title: Fix ArcSwap rcu() to derive 'swap applied' from the return value, not a closure-mutated variable

invented_rule.summary: When using arc-swap's rcu() for a conditional atomic swap, the 'was applied' outcome must be derived from rcu()'s return value (the previous Arc), never from a variable mutated inside the closure, which can run multiple times under CAS contention.
invented_rule.absent_from_pretraining_rationale: The arc-swap crate's rcu() CAS retry loop behavior — that the closure can run multiple times, making external mutation of 'applied' flags unreliable — is a crate-specific quirk discovered through debugging this project's snapshot update path. Generic Rust concurrency best-practices do not cover arc-swap's CAS retry semantics, and a pretrained model would likely accept the mutated-bool pattern as correct since it looks syntactically valid.

verifier.contract: Invoked as `<command> <workspace_dir>`. Exit 0 == invented rule OBEYED (task win). Non-zero == rule NOT obeyed. MUST print a one-line human reason to stdout. NO network, NO LLM — pure deterministic inspection of the produced workspace/diff.

expected.sensitivity_note: If ON fails this with the rule injected (attribution confirms the pull), that is INSTRUMENT-FAILURE.
